title: FILTER vs VLOOKUP: return every match, not just the first
meta_desc: FILTER vs VLOOKUP: single vs multiple results, spill behavior, left-lookups, and verified compatibility across Excel, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice.
intro: VLOOKUP finds the first row that matches and returns one value. FILTER returns every row that matches, spilling them into a range. If a key can appear more than once — all orders for a customer, all students in a class — VLOOKUP silently drops the rest and FILTER is what you actually want.

cols: A whole range/array you can shape
No — lookup column must be leftmost
No — needs a helper column or XLOOKUP
Sheets: all; Excel 365 & LibreOffice 24.8+ (see the FILTER page)
Universal — documented across all three; executed in every LibreOffice version we test

when.use_when: One key maps to one value and you just need that value — a price for a SKU, a name for an ID. It's universal, so it's the portable choice for older Excel or shared files.

A key can match many rows and you need them all, you want to pull columns to the left of the key, or you need multi-condition logic. Modern Sheets/Excel only — check the compat note before shipping to old Excel.

compat_note: VLOOKUP runs everywhere; FILTER is newer — native in all Google Sheets, but Excel needs 365 (dynamic arrays) and LibreOffice needs 24.8+. On a version without FILTER it errors as #NAME?, so for files that may open in old Excel, stick with VLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH or gate on the version. Where both exist, FILTER also sidesteps VLOOKUP's leftmost-column limitation and its silent 'first match only' behavior.
